# BlinkSend

> Fast, free, peer-to-peer file and clipboard sharing between phones and computers. No account needed.

Repository: https://github.com/ghostySRC/BlinkSend
Default branch: main
License: MIT
Runtime: Node.js 20+, browser JavaScript, WebRTC data channels

## Product model

BlinkSend is a two-peer, self-hosted transfer app. The Node.js server serves the application, coordinates WebRTC signaling, generates QR codes, issues protected short-lived ICE/TURN credentials, and optionally maintains five-minute Nearby discovery metadata. Normal file contents travel over the WebRTC data channel rather than through the application server.

## Main capabilities

- simple Send / Receive entry flow
- invite-link pairing, QR generation, in-app QR scanning, and opt-in Nearby discovery
- optional local device names
- mutual six-digit peer verification derived from WebRTC DTLS fingerprints
- SHA-256 file verification with bounded per-file retry
- browser-safe numbered chunks plus chunk bitmap / missing-range resume
- same-tab reconnect and restart-safe resume on supported File System Access browsers
- File System Access and OPFS large-file streaming
- folder transfer, recursive drag-and-drop, and nested folder reconstruction
- clipboard/text transfer up to 256 KB using small UTF-8 control frames
- paste-to-send for clipboard files/images/text
- automatic 512 KiB connection calibration, adaptive WebRTC buffering, Direct/Relay quality, smoothed speed, ETA, and batch progress
- network-interface ICE recovery
- local-only transfer history and optional completion feedback
- Web Share for received files/text
- installable PWA and local Web Share Target staging
- English/Swedish and light/dark UI
- rate-limited signaling, protected TURN credential access, and malformed-message controls

## Important files

- README.md — current product behavior, setup, architecture, deployment, limits, tests
- SECURITY.md — threat model and vulnerability reporting
- AGENTS.md — coding-agent invariants
- server.js — HTTP server, signaling, QR, Nearby, ICE/TURN and abuse controls
- public/index.html — UI
- public/app.js — pairing, WebRTC transfer protocol, resume, batching and UX state
- public/protocol.js — pure transfer helpers: tuning, ETA, range maps, path validation, UTF-8 framing
- public/sha256.js — incremental SHA-256
- public/persistence.js — IndexedDB transfer sessions and local history
- public/manifest.webmanifest — PWA and Share Target metadata
- public/sw.js — PWA shell cache and local Share Target interception
- scripts/benchmark.mjs — deterministic 5 GiB-equivalent chunk-map / 10k-file benchmark
- test/ — signaling, security, integrity, protocol, PWA and stress tests
- .github/workflows/ci.yml — CI

## Development

```bash
npm ci
npm test
npm run bench
npm start
```

Open http://localhost:3000.

## Transfer invariants

1. Exactly two WebSocket peers may occupy a room.
2. Transfer UI remains locked until mutual fingerprint-code confirmation.
3. File payloads use WebRTC data channels; the application server should not receive normal file contents.
4. Every completed file must match SHA-256 before being reported as verified.
5. Incoming relative paths are normalized and traversal segments are rejected.
6. Resume state may request missing chunk ranges; persisted handles are capability-dependent.
7. Nearby discovery is opt-in, same-observed-address scoped, short-lived, and never replaces fingerprint verification.
8. Share Target payloads remain device-local until they enter the normal P2P flow.

## Browser capability notes

Feature availability depends on browser APIs including File System Access, OPFS, BarcodeDetector, Web Share / Share Target, service workers, IndexedDB, and WebRTC. Maintain graceful fallbacks instead of assuming Chromium-only APIs.

## AI / coding-agent guidance

Read README.md, SECURITY.md, AGENTS.md, server.js, public/app.js, public/protocol.js, public/persistence.js, and relevant tests before protocol changes. Preserve the security invariants above. Update README.md in the same logical change as user-visible behavior and add tests for protocol/security changes.
